sources.title: Interview note containing the odd/even-position linked-list sorting problem and intended solution direction
Deterministic Java validation against an independent full-sort oracle with node-identity checks
Source-first isolated review for the odd/even monotonic linked-list candidate

claims.text: The recovered source states that odd-position nodes are in ascending order, even-position nodes are in descending order, the two subsequences have no cross-order relationship, and the target is O(n) time with O(1) extra space.
The source itself records the intended split odd/even positions, reverse the even-position list, then merge the two ordered lists direction.

Splitting preserves each positional subsequence, reversing the nonincreasing even-position subsequence makes it nondecreasing, and standard two-way merge then yields one globally nondecreasing list containing all nodes.
Split, reverse and merge are each linear passes and the implementation uses only a constant number of node references, so the algorithm runs in O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary space.

The exact Java implementation passes nine fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized valid-input lists against an independent full-sort oracle while preserving node identities, node count and acyclicity.

checks: odd-position nondecreasing and even-position nonincreasing inputs
null-equivalent empty list and single node
acyclic output and unchanged node count

boundary_tests.expected: result remains globally nondecreasing and retains every original node
ordering uses int comparison without arithmetic overflow dependence

findings: The candidate preserves the exact positional monotonicity contract and source-recorded solution direction.
The split/reverse/merge invariants and complexity claims are checked by deterministic differential testing and node-identity assertions.
API behavior absent from the source is labelled as a candidate choice.
No unsupported personal or project claims are present.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the human-approval gate.
